name: checkout
description: Action for checking out a repo
one_liner: The standard building block that grabs your code at the start of almost every GitHub automation workflow.
buyer: No one. This is plumbing every GitHub Actions user already relies on for free. It trends whenever a new major version ships.
business_use_cases: A team pins the new version to keep their CI pipelines secure and working.
There is no product to build here; it's a dependency, not an opportunity.
The only lesson worth taking: security-hardening releases (like its safer fork-PR handling) drive attention, a reminder that CI security is a real, sellable concern elsewhere.

money_ideas.idea: Nothing to sell around this directly. If anything, the adjacent opportunity is CI-security auditing services for teams who never update their actions.

steal_this: Don't build on this. Do go check that your own workflows are on the latest, secure version. That's the actionable takeaway.
